title: Introduce per-route seasonal baselines and request-shape clustering for adaptive alert calibration
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We see repeated bursts and predictable weekly/diurnal patterns per-route that make static SLO thresholds noisy (false positives during predictable peaks, and missed regressions during troughs). Existing per-route percentiles don't account for seasonality and multimodal request shapes (short prompts vs long multi-turn sessions), which leads to noisy alerts and manual tuning. This PR introduces a lightweight baseline generator that decomposes per-route token-cost and latency time series into seasonal + trend + residual components, and a complementary request-shape clustering pipeline so we compute baselines and alert thresholds per route x shape instead of a single global route threshold.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds a seasonal-trend decomposition service (stl-lite) that runs incremental updates on per-route per-hour rollups and emits a stable baseline median and a seasonal amplitude metric. The algorithm is a compact STL-inspired decomposition optimized for streaming rollups (low memory, O(n) incremental).
- Introduces request-shape fingerprinting (prompt_length_bucket, kv_cache_hit_rate_bucket, streaming_tokens_flag, model_variant) and a clustering stage that assigns a route request to a small integer cluster id (0..N-1). Clustering is done by mini-batch k-means on compact sketch features with daily re-fit.
- Calibrator component that computes adaptive alert thresholds per (route,shape_cluster) using robust quantiles of the residual distribution combined with a sigmoid smoothing factor that prevents alerts on short, transient spikes. Calibration parameters are stored in the config store and surfaced to Alerting and Console.
- Low-cardinality metric exports and trace enrichment: emits aggregated histograms keyed by route and cluster id (rwi.route.shape.histogram) and annotates top-level spans with shape tags (rwi.route.shape_cluster) for downstream joins. To avoid cardinality explosion we keep cluster ids dense and only enable shape tags for routes with >100 requests/day by default.
- Console additions: new dashboard panels (Route Shape Explorer, Clustered Baseline Overview, Residual Anomaly Streams) and an alert tuning UI that exposes the calibrator's sigmoid and quantile parameters per route.

Why this is different: Rather than raising global per-route thresholds or trying to tune many static alerts, this approach models predictable seasonality and the multimodal structure of traffic so alerts can be both more sensitive to true regressions and less noisy. The design intentionally minimizes cardinality and CPU overhead so it is safe to roll out as a tenant-facing feature.

Implementation notes:
- New service: observations/calibrator (go). Uses a streaming rollup input (hourly route x cluster rollups) and writes baseline rows to telemetry.baselines (compact protobuf payload).
- New metrics: rwi_route_shape_bucket (histogram labels: route, cluster_id), rwi_baseline_median_tokens (gauge), rwi_baseline_seasonal_amp (gauge), rwi_calibrator_score (gauge).
- Tracing: top-level server span now includes tags: route.shape_cluster (int), route.shape_signature (hash). Only added when route sampling flag is enabled to protect cardinality.
- Safe defaults and feature flags: feature gate observability.route_shape_clustering=false by default. Canary rollout configured in infra/defaults.yaml (10% tenants, 4-hour ramp).

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for the STL-lite decomposition (edge cases: sparse hours, daylight savings transitions) and for clustering stability (minibatch seed determinism).
- Integration tests: simulated workloads with two synthetic routes (short-chat vs long-batch) validate per-cluster baselines and expected alert suppression on seasonal peaks.
- Performance: local profiling shows the calibrator service uses <5% CPU on a c4-large equivalent with the default 10k-route config. Metric cardinality increases were measured <2.3% in a 2-week canary.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag.
2) Enable for 10% tenants (canary group) for 72 hours and monitor rwi_calibrator_score distributions and SLO alert counts.
3) If stable, ramp to 50% and enable dashboard UI in read-only mode.
4) After 2 weeks of stable behavior, flip write-enable so calibrator can update alert thresholds and expose full UI.

Backward compat and migration:
- No breaking API changes. Baseline rows are additive and ignored by older services.
- Migration job included (tools/migrate/compact_baselines) to backfill 30 days of baseline statistics for existing routes. Backfill is optional but recommended for teams enabling the calibrator.

Related work: Linear: ENG-2049, SRE-778. See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2049/route-shape-clustering-and-seasonal-baselines (internal link).

Checklist: implemented code, unit + integration tests, migration script, console panels, feature flag, changelog entry, performance safety review signed off.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Nice end-to-end. A few nitpicks: can we cap seasonal amplitude so a runaway route doesn't push thresholds too high? Also please add more metrics around calibration failure/retries.
Maya Chen (author): Added amplitude cap and two new health metrics (calibrator.up and calibrator.recent_backfills). Updated tests to cover amplitude cap.
Leah Kim: Please document how cluster ids are stable across daily refits. Concerned about alert churn if cluster mapping flips frequently.
Maya Chen: Cluster assignment stabilized via hashed seed + drift smoothing; added explanation and an instrumented metric cluster.reassign_rate.

Diego Morales: Verified console panels render correctly in chrome and firefox. Approving once CI is green. 
(approved)
release_notes: Add per-route seasonal baselines and request-shape clustering to reduce noisy alerts and provide adaptive per-cluster thresholds; feature gated and rolled out as a canary.
